items.title: Depeche Mode puts Indira Paganotto’s ‘People Are Good’ remix on streaming
items.summary: Depeche Mode has put Indira Paganotto's "People Are Good" remix on streaming, ahead of the 7LP Memento Mori box set due January 27, 2027.
items.fullText:
Depeche Mode has made the Indira Paganotto Psy Remix of “People Are Good” available on streaming platforms. The track went up on Spotify on November 18, 2026, under exclusive license to Columbia Records, a division of Sony Music Entertainment. Until now it had circulated only on 12-inch vinyl, and it is confirmed as one of 41 tracks on the forthcoming box set Memento Mori | The 12″ Singles, a 7 x 12″ EP UK vinyl collection due January 27, 2027 on Mute, Columbia and Sony Music.

“People Are Good” is track nine on Depeche Mode’s fifteenth studio album, “Memento Mori” (Columbia, released March 24, 2023), written by Martin L. Gore with lead vocals by Dave Gahan. Columbia issued it as the album’s seventh single on April 5, 2024, paired with a five-track remix EP by Alessandro Cortini, Ludwig A.F., SiGNL, Obskur and Indira Paganotto, and an official video directed by Rich Hall with creative direction by Anton Corbijn. That digital EP carried only one of Paganotto’s two remixes, the Twilight Remix. Her Psy Remix stayed exclusive to the 12-inch single “Before We Drown / People Are Good (Remixes),” the final release in the band’s 2023-2024 Memento Mori White Label Remix Series, a run of limited, individually numbered vinyl singles that began with “Ghosts Again” in November 2023.

Memento Mori | The 12″ Singles gathers that series, plus the preceding singles “Ghosts Again,” “Wagging Tongue,” “My Favourite Stranger” and “Before We Drown,” across 12 sides. Two further sides carry session recordings: the Memento Mori Sessions versions of “Survive,” “Life 2.0,” “Give Yourself to Me” and “In the End,” and the Vinegar Hill Sessions versions of “Ghosts Again,” “Wagging Tongue” and “My Favourite Stranger,” stripped-back takes recorded at the Vinegar Hill studio in Brooklyn. The box includes a download card for uncompressed 16-bit WAV files of every track and a replica UK promo poster for “Ghosts Again.” The set is listed for pre-order as a 7 x 12″ EP vinyl box through Sony Music’s online store.

About Depeche Mode

Depeche Mode formed in Basildon, Essex, England, in 1980, originally as Composition of Sound with Vince Clarke on vocals and guitar and Andy Fletcher on bass, soon joined by Martin Gore on guitar and Dave Gahan on vocals. The group took the name Depeche Mode that September and released its debut single, “Dreaming of Me,” on Mute Records in February 1981, followed by the album “Speak & Spell” that October. Clarke left at the end of 1981 to form Yazoo and later Erasure. Gore became the band’s chief songwriter. Alan Wilder joined in 1982 and remained the band’s fourth member through “Construction Time Again” (1983), “Some Great Reward” (1984, featuring “People Are People”), “Black Celebration” (1986) and “Music for the Masses” (1987). “Violator” (1990) brought the international hits “Personal Jesus” and “Enjoy the Silence,” and “Songs of Faith and Devotion” (1993) topped the UK and US album charts before Wilder left in 1995.

Gahan, Gore and Fletcher continued as a trio through “Ultra” (1997), “Exciter” (2001), “Playing the Angel” (2005), “Sounds of the Universe” (2009), “Delta Machine” (2013) and “Spirit” (2017), signing to Columbia Records for Delta Machine. The band was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2020. Fletcher died on May 26, 2022, and Gahan and Gore have continued as a duo, releasing the band’s fifteenth studio album, “Memento Mori,” produced by James Ford, on March 24, 2023. Its singles included Ghosts Again, co-written with Richard Butler of the Psychedelic Furs, and the album was supported by a 112-show Memento Mori World Tour that ran into April 2024. Depeche Mode’s most recent original recording is a cover of “Universal Soldier” for War Child’s “Help(2)” charity album, released March 6, 2026. The Psy Remix’s arrival on streaming closes the last digital gap in the Memento Mori White Label Remix Series, two months ahead of Memento Mori | The 12″ Singles gathering the full run on vinyl.

items.title: “Reflections in the Night” — Turkish Darkwave Duo Ductape Hold Moonlight in Their Hands in Video for “D.E.R.T”
items.summary: In a crowded place I’m still unknown Dancing lights, reflections in the night Empty room just messes with my mind The beat goes on Modern civilization has become a magnificent… The post “Reflections in the Night” — Turkish Darkwave Duo Ductape Hold Moonlight i
items.fullText:
In a crowded place I’m still unknown
Dancing lights, reflections in the night
Empty room just messes with my mind
The beat goes on

Modern civilization has become a magnificent assembly line of manufactured personalities, where everybody gets to be an individual provided they purchase the correct uniform, subscribe to the appropriate ideology, and maintain a sufficiently attractive digital representation of their miserable little existence. Meanwhile, the dancefloors are packed, the algorithms are thriving, and loneliness has apparently become humanity’s most reliable growth industry. Somewhere in this enormous psychological junkyard, Turkish post-punk duo Ductape have decided to examine the wreckage with their new album, Faded Flowers.

The title imagines humanity as a field of dying flowers, each individual slowly drained by repetition, conformity, and the exhausting business of pretending everything is perfectly wonderful. With fierce synthesizers, cold, commanding basslines, and Furkan’s wonderfully agitated guitar work, Ductape approach this collective nervous breakdown with considerable conviction. His guitar lines argue, interrupt, plead, and occasionally sound ready to file a formal complaint against the entire human race, while Çağla’s commanding vocals move between icy composure and emotional urgency.

D.E.R.T. carries these anxieties into a wonderfully strange visual territory. The video, filmed in grainy black-and-white by Begüm Koçum, moves between sunlit fields and stark portraits against a pitch-black backdrop. Elaborate clothing, sharply drawn makeup, and tightly framed gestures suggest a world where identity has become an elaborate theatrical production, complete with costumes, poses, and absolutely no guarantee that anyone knows their lines.

The lyrics address the absurd contradiction of feeling utterly alone in a room full of people. Music continues, bodies move, and everybody participates in the great social masquerade, yet genuine recognition remains frustratingly elusive. Beneath the insistent beat lies an existential question about authenticity and what it actually means to feel alive.

Then comes the enormous, roughly textured white sphere, resembling a moon that somebody has stolen from the heavens and brought along for moral support. Passed between Çağla and Furkan, it becomes an enigmatic object of shared concern, affection, and possibly cosmic responsibility. Clasped hands, intertwined bodies, and an outstretched sleeve connecting the musicians introduce moments of genuine tenderness amid the visual austerity. These gestures suggest that intimacy might offer some resistance to the machinery of alienation.

Watch the video for D.E.R.T below:

Throughout Faded Flowers, the duo take aim at contemporary society’s collection of false gods: institutional authority, manufactured ideals, rigid expectations, and the digital identities we dutifully polish while our actual personalities quietly disintegrate. The rhythms maintain their relentless forward momentum, giving the album the peculiar sensation of dancing through a civilization that has apparently misplaced its operating instructions. With Faded Flowers, Ductape offer a beautifully bruised examination of contemporary existence, where humanity keeps dancing despite having precious little idea why, and the possibility of connection remains worth fighting for.

items.fullText:
Klayton released “No Damage” as Celldweller on 18 November 2026, the third single from his sixth studio album, “GOD MODE,” via his own label FiXT. The song follows the singles “Fakebreaker,” featuring SWARM and REEBZ, and “Respawn.”

Klayton said the track began as a demo for his FreqGen project, built around the atmospheric jungle and drum & bass of the early PlayStation era, citing Goldie, Aphrodite, LTJ Bukem and High Contrast as reference points, before he added guitars and folded it into “GOD MODE.” Blending alternative metal, nu metal and hard rock with that drum & bass foundation, “No Damage” addresses betrayal and the struggle to stay standing when trust has been broken, built around the line “set your crosshairs on my heart, this mortal coil blown apart, but I’ll take no damage.” Klayton also directed the lyric video himself at Blackstar, his new Detroit studio, filming a wall of CRT televisions through hardware glitch effects.

“No Damage” is available to stream on all major platforms via FiXT. Season Pass holders on EVEN get early access to further “GOD MODE” singles and bonus tracks.

About Celldweller

Celldweller is the primary recording project of producer Klayton, who also records as Scandroid and Circle of Dust and founded the independent label FiXT in 2006 with James Rhodes. The self-titled “Celldweller” album arrived in 2003, followed by “Wish Upon a Blackstar” in 2012, “End of an Empire” in 2015, “Offworld” in 2017 and “Satellites” in 2022. Klayton’s music has appeared in releases and placements including Westworld, Suicide Squad, Deadpool, John Wick and Call of Duty.

“GOD MODE,” Celldweller’s sixth studio album, has so far been previewed by the singles “Respawn” and “Fakebreaker” featuring SWARM and REEBZ. Klayton also opened the “Thief: Pulse of Promise” soundtrack with the Celldweller track “Never a Thief” in August 2026. “No Damage” continues the album’s rollout as its third single.

items.title: Secrecy releases debut EP ‘Winter In A&E’
items.summary: London post-punk band Secrecy release their debut recorded outing, "Winter In A&E," a six-track mini-LP on La Vida Es Un Mus Discos.
items.fullText:
London post-punk band Secrecy has released its debut recorded outing, “Winter In A&E,” a six-track mini-LP out now on La Vida Es Un Mus Discos. The release was produced and recorded by Ski and Rob Hammerén at Ray’s Studio in London.

“Winter In A&E” runs six tracks: “Knife in My Dreams,” “You’ll Get What You Want,” “Boys and Girls,” “Virgins,” “Powder Reaper” and the title track. The band draws on the martial drive of Killing Joke, the post-punk of The Execute and Southern Death Cult, and the guitar work of The Chameleons, with vocals in the vein of Blitz’s “Second Empire Justice.” Stanley Gravett mixed the record at Holy Mountain, with mastering by Nik Kozub; artwork and layout are by Volodea Biri, with photography by James Burgess.

“Winter In A&E” is available now via Bandcamp. Secrecy plays a release show on 3 December, with venue details to be announced, followed by a London date at Hootananny Brixton on 18 February 2027, supporting Synthicide with Aurat, Eddie Dark and DJ Fil Noir.

About Secrecy

Secrecy is a post-punk band from London, known locally for its live shows before releasing any recorded material. “Winter In A&E,” the band’s debut mini-LP, was produced and recorded by Ski and Rob Hammerén at Ray’s Studio, London, mixed by Stanley Gravett at Holy Mountain, and mastered by Nik Kozub.

The EP’s six songs move through romantic dependency, revenge, religious imagery and hospital-ward imagery, closing on the title track. Secrecy follows the release with a release show on 3 December and a London date at Hootananny Brixton on 18 February 2027.

items.title: CTRL CLICK unveils video for ‘Angel of Death’
items.summary: CTRL CLICK releases a video for "Angel of Death," the opening track from debut album "Systems for Disassembly," out now on Negative Gain.
items.fullText:
Rockford, Illinois industrial project CTRL CLICK, the work of Eric Nofsinger, has released a video for “Angel of Death,” the opening track from debut album “Systems for Disassembly.” Side-Line reported on the album’s 6 November release date in October; it is now out on CD and digital formats through Negative Gain Productions.

“Angel of Death” opens over mechanical drones, metallic clanks and a spoken repetition of the title before a machine-driven snare sets its tempo. The video follows a succession of near-monochrome hospital rooms and corridors, where a white-winged figure moves through shots intercut with an ECG trace, surgical instruments and an IV bag. Large lyrics tilt and break across the images as the song treats death as a quiet, procedural presence, not a dramatic one.

“Systems for Disassembly” runs fourteen tracks, including “Insolent,” “Good as Dead,” “Our God,” “Slip Up” and closer “(Kill) the Vampire,” built around themes of employment, addiction, surveillance and institutional control. Nofsinger produced and mixed the album himself, with mastering by Rob Robinson of Kevorkian Death Cycle and ohGr.

“Systems for Disassembly” is available now on CD and digital formats via Negative Gain Productions.

About CTRL CLICK

CTRL CLICK is the industrial project of Rockford, Illinois artist Eric Nofsinger. Before recording as CTRL CLICK, Nofsinger spent three decades in video games, joining High Voltage Software in 1994 as its first artist and helping grow the studio to 185 developers working on titles including Fortnite, Mortal Kombat X and Baldur’s Gate: Dark Alliance, leading its creative work through the studio’s 2020 sale to Keywords Studios.

CTRL CLICK’s debut album, “Systems for Disassembly,” was announced in October for a 6 November release on Negative Gain Productions. Nofsinger produced and mixed the record himself, with mastering by Rob Robinson of Kevorkian Death Cycle and ohGr. “Angel of Death,” the album’s opening track, is the first single to receive a video.

items.title: Metamourne unveil video for ‘Dance, Baby’
items.summary: Perth darkwave duo Metamourne release a video for "Dance, Baby," the second single from their forthcoming EP "Mors Certa," due in 2027.
items.fullText:
Perth, Western Australia darkwave duo Metamourne have released a video for “Dance, Baby,” the second single from their forthcoming second EP, provisionally titled “Mors Certa.” The track combines darkwave with heavier gothic rock, and arrived on Bandcamp on 11 November.

“Dance, Baby” is the work of vocalist and lyricist Ross MacRae and musician and producer Martin Murphy, mixed by Brendan Dekora. Murphy cites AFI’s “Holy Visions” and the chorus guitar pattern of Rammstein’s “Zwitter” as influences on the track, which centres on a consensual chase between two people negotiating control and surrender. Murphy described the song’s themes directly: “Beneath the imagery of hunting and possession lies an exploration of obsession and the paradox of finding control in willingness to give it away.”

Shot in black and white across four locations, the video was directed and filmed by Murphy, who began it as Instagram material shot in his apartment’s storage area before expanding it into the duo’s first full-length DIY video. It follows a pursuit through a storage corridor and an open field, ending with the captive turning the tables on her captors. Photography for the release came from Murphy under the name DoYouKnowMadMax.

“Dance, Baby” follows September’s single “Grave Walker” as the second release from “Mors Certa,” which Metamourne is targeting for an early-to-mid-2027 release. The single is available now via Bandcamp.

About Metamourne

Metamourne is a darkwave and gothic rock duo from Perth, Western Australia, formed in October 2025 by vocalist and lyricist Ross MacRae and musician and producer Martin Murphy. Both musicians came to the project after years in metal bands, turning toward post-punk and darkwave for their shared material. The band’s name combines “meta,” the polyamorous term for a partner’s partner, with a reference to mourning.

Metamourne released its debut EP, “Nocturne Minuet,” in May 2026. The duo followed it with the single “Grave Walker” in September and “Dance, Baby” in November, both drawn from a forthcoming second EP, provisionally titled “Mors Certa” and targeted for an early-to-mid-2027 release. “Dance, Baby” arrives with the duo’s first full-length music video, directed by Murphy.

items.title: Twin Cynic releases debut album ‘Identity Crisis’
items.summary: Bristol project Twin Cynic, the solo work of TJ Higgs, releases debut album "Identity Crisis," eleven tracks of synth-driven post-punk and darkwave.
items.fullText:
Bristol project Twin Cynic, the solo work of musician TJ Higgs, has released its debut album, “Identity Crisis,” on 29 October. The eleven-track record moves through synth-driven post-punk, darkwave and alternative rock, with Higgs handling both guitar and synthesizer parts.

The tracklist runs “Star Fairy,” “Cinema,” “Sin By Silence,” “Stardust,” “People Are People,” “At The Masquerade,” “Cherry And Almond,” “Terpsichore,” “Howling At The Moon,” “North Star” and “Beautiful Nonsense.” “People Are People” is a cover of the 1984 Depeche Mode single, reworked with a heavier guitar presence under its original drum pattern and brass-like synthesizer lines. Higgs, who spent years performing in metal bands before turning to post-punk and darkwave, lets that history shape the album’s riffing, while the songs themselves take on identity, alienation, grief and desire.

“Identity Crisis” is available now as a digital album on Bandcamp. Twin Cynic plays The Old England in Bristol on 28 November, supporting PitFeeders.

About Twin Cynic

Bristol musician TJ Higgs records as Twin Cynic. Before turning to synth-driven post-punk and darkwave, he spent years performing in metal bands, a background audible in the guitar weight running through his newer material.

“Identity Crisis,” released 29 October 2026, is Twin Cynic’s debut album. Its eleven songs include a cover of Depeche Mode’s “People Are People” alongside original material addressing grief, performance, desire and mortality. Higgs follows the album’s release with a Bristol date at The Old England on 28 November, supporting PitFeeders.

items.title: Twin Ion Engine release third album ‘(III) Midsummer Lover’
items.summary: San Diego post-punk and darkwave duo Twin Ion Engine release their third album, "(III) Midsummer Lover," led by Eddie Lopez.

San Diego post-punk and darkwave project Twin Ion Engine have released their third studio album, “(III) Midsummer Lover.” Founder Eddie Lopez recorded and produced the record himself, bringing in collaborators Jo Esq and Ghost Days for a release centred on romantic attachment and its fallout.

The album’s musical vocabulary draws on the basslines of European post-punk, the momentum of darkwave and the melodic instincts of early-2000s indie rock. Twin Ion Engine began in 2020 as the solo project of Lopez before growing into its current duo format.

“(III) Midsummer Lover” is available now via Bandcamp and other streaming platforms, with a 12-inch vinyl edition available to pre-order.

About Twin Ion Engine

Twin Ion Engine is a San Diego, California post-punk and darkwave project founded in 2020 as the solo enterprise of Eddie Lopez. The project has since grown into a duo, with Lopez recording and producing its releases himself and bringing in outside collaborators, including Jo Esq and Ghost Days, for individual records.

“(III) Midsummer Lover,” the project’s third studio album, follows that collaborative approach, with Lopez again handling production. The record continues Twin Ion Engine’s run of self-released music on Bandcamp, where the band also issues singles and collaborations alongside its full-length albums.

items.title: The Spiritual Bat unveil video for ‘Theatre of Dust’
items.summary: The Spiritual Bat release a video for "Theatre of Dust," the title track of their album of the same name, out now on Swiss Dark Nights.
items.fullText:
Italian gothic rock band The Spiritual Bat have released a video for “Theatre of Dust”, the title track of their album of the same name, out now on Swiss Dark Nights. Filmed, edited and directed by Laura Rossi, who co-wrote the concept with vocalist Rosetta Garrì, the video follows a woman fleeing an oppressive barrage of news for forests, stone settlements and underground passages, where other seekers searching for an elusive truth gradually join her.

The band describes the song as a journey “through barren lands and cliff edges, questioning where sanity ends and awakening begins.” “Theatre of Dust” is the collaboration of vocalist and lyricist Rosetta Garrì, guitarist Dario Passamonti and producer and drummer Doc Hammer of Requiem in White, who also produced and mixed the eight-track album at his Goat of Brass Studio in New York.

The Spiritual Bat play Milan on 28 November with Scarlet and the Spooky Spiders, a New Year’s Eve show in Rouen on 31 December, and three Finnish dates in April 2027:

  • November 28, 2026 – Milan, Italy – C.I.Q. (with Scarlet and the Spooky Spiders)
  • December 31, 2026 – Rouen, France – La Crypte Rosa†Crvx
  • April 2, 2027 – Helsinki, Finland – Lepakkomies (with Fenetzar and Aus Tears)
  • April 3, 2027 – Turku, Finland – Nirvana (with Shocked Volk and Hateful Chains)
  • April 4, 2027 – Tampere, Finland – venue to be announced

About The Spiritual Bat

The Spiritual Bat is a deathrock and gothic rock band from Italy, conceived in 1992 by songwriter Dario Passamonti and singer Matteo Bracaglia as Spiritual BatS. The project released a self-titled EP in 1993, followed by its first full-length album, “Confession,” in 1996. The lineup later centred on Passamonti and singer Rosetta Garrì.

Further albums followed, including “Sacrament” in 1999, “Through the Shadows” in 2008, “Cruel Machine” in 2011 and “Your Own World (And the Vision of Sound)” in 2017. The band is signed to Swiss Dark Nights, which Side-Line covered as it issued an early single from the “Mission: Create” album in 2022, the same year the label also released the retrospective boxset “Origins and Transmutations”, gathering material from the band’s back catalogue.

“Theatre of Dust,” released 31 August 2026, continues the Swiss Dark Nights partnership and is the band’s first album made with Doc Hammer in the studio. Its eight songs take in “Creatures,” “All My Power,” “Black Fields,” “Babylon Now,” “A Darker Gaze,” the title track, “Hello Heartache” and closer “Anti Matter,” for which the band also issued a video. The video for “Theatre of Dust” follows that release and continues the band’s international touring, which has included Wave-Gotik-Treffen, Whitby Goth Weekend, Return to the Batcave, Castle Party and New York’s Red Party.

items.title: Odonis Odonis return with ‘No One Is Coming to Save You’ single
items.summary: Odonis Odonis release "No One Is Coming to Save You," the first single from upcoming seventh album "A Fractured Future," due in 2027 on After Hours Records.
items.fullText:
Toronto electronic project Odonis Odonis has released “No One Is Coming to Save You”, the first single from its upcoming seventh album, “A Fractured Future.” The track arrived on Bandcamp on 17 November, with the album due sometime in 2027 on a new imprint, After Hours Records, founded by the project’s core member, Constantin Tzenos.

The track’s origins lie in DISORDER, a dark dance night Tzenos produced with Dwight Hybrid, who also contributes production, lyrics and vocals to the song. “I wanted something that would work at 1am in that room, so I wrote it around the floor first: a hard kick, industrial-darkwave synths and a hook you can shout back,” Tzenos said. “We knew it clicked the first time we dropped it on the dance floor.”

Odonis Odonis is now the solo vehicle of Tzenos, following a 2025 self-titled album the band described as a reflective, moody affair. “No One Is Coming To Save You” turns toward acid house, italo and horror-club territory, while keeping what the band calls its trademark industrial aggression. Tzenos described the lyrics as a call to self-reliance: “Nobody’s coming to fix this. Not the government, not the algorithm. If you want the world back from the vampires, you have to take it yourself.”

“No One Is Coming To Save You” is available via Bandcamp and streaming platforms.

About Odonis Odonis

Odonis Odonis is a Toronto electronic project founded by Constantin Tzenos, active for 15 years across a catalogue that has moved between psychedelic dream pop, industrial cyberpunk and the spaces between. The band’s past releases include the album “Icon” and, most recently, a 2025 self-titled record. Tzenos also co-produces DISORDER, a dark dance night in Toronto with Dwight Hybrid, who joins him on “No One Is Coming To Save You” as co-writer and vocalist.

Now working as a solo vehicle for Tzenos, Odonis Odonis follows “No One Is Coming To Save You” with a seventh album, “A Fractured Future,” set for release sometime in 2027 on Tzenos’ own new label, After Hours Records.

items.title: Digital Energy – Echoes Of Tomorrow (Digital/CD Album – Infacted Recordings)

Founded in 2000 as a duo, put on hold between 2009 and 2014, and returning—now as a solo project helmed by David Erdmann—this German act has arrived at its latest album. For this release, Gerrit Thomas (Funker Vogt, Eisfabrik, Fictional) was brought on board as producer.

The result is a classic-leaning Electro-Pop production that evokes influences from Depeche Mode, and—perhaps even more so—De/Vision. The tracks benefit from a strong, polished production, which gives them a powerful, driving quality. This is further enhanced by prominent lead melodies that introduce a distinct Trance-like element. Rather than mere ‘power-pop’, this is a mature production that not only elevates the sound but also manifests in expertly crafted choruses that anchor each song. Naturally, a high-quality Electro-Pop production requires a talented vocalist, and that is certainly the case here.

Until now, Digital Energy hadn’t left a particularly strong impression, but with “Echoes Of Tomorrow,” a new era seems to have begun. In my view, this is a highly recommended release! (Rating:8).

About Digital Energy

Digital Energy formed in Germany in 2000 as a duo of David Erdmann (vocals, music) and Bernd Kupke (lyrics, music). The project went on hiatus between 2009 and 2014 before the pair resumed working together. Kupke left Digital Energy in June 2025, and Erdmann has continued the project alone since.

Early albums, including “Illusion” (2000) and “Somehow I Miss You” (2003), were self-released. items.title: San Diego Post-Punk Duo Twin Ion Engine Explores Romance and Ruin on Third Album “(III) Midsummer Lover”
items.summary: Romance is a magnificent form of voluntary insanity, a condition in which otherwise sensible people surrender their dignity to somebody who might eventually leave them standing in the kitchen at… The post San Diego Post-Punk Duo Twin Ion Engine Explores Romanc
items.fullText:
Romance is a magnificent form of voluntary insanity, a condition in which otherwise sensible people surrender their dignity to somebody who might eventually leave them standing in the kitchen at three in the morning, contemplating the emotional significance of an unanswered text message. Love makes idiots of intellectuals, poets of drunks, and philosophers of people who previously struggled to articulate anything more complicated than their lunch order. Fortunately, popular music has spent the better part of a century documenting this widespread psychological malfunction, and San Diego’s TWIN ION ENGINE have arrived with another contribution to the grand catalogue of catastrophe.

Founded in 2020 as the solitary musical enterprise of Eddie Lopez, TWIN ION ENGINE have grown into a post-punk and darkwave duo whose third studio album, (III) Midsummer Lover, explores the complicated business of wanting somebody, losing somebody, and occasionally wondering why anybody bothers with emotional attachments when solitary confinement seems considerably less exhausting.

Lopez recorded and produced the album himself, bringing collaborators Jo Esq and Ghost Days into a project whose musical vocabulary draws upon the stern basslines of European post-punk, the mechanical momentum of darkwave, and the melodic instincts of early-2000s indie rock. The guitars carry a romantic tension reminiscent of Twin Tribes, Early Cure, and The Chameleons, while the bass recalls the relentless forward movement associated with Molchat Doma. There are traces of Lebanon Hanover in the restrained vocal delivery, though Lopez appears equally interested in the possibilities of a good hook, allowing melody to interfere with the business of being miserable. That combination makes considerable sense. After all, romantic desperation has always benefited from a decent rhythm section, particularly when the alternative involves sitting alone with your thoughts and discovering how extraordinarily unpleasant your own company can become.

The title itself suggests an affection for romance in all its irrational glory. Summer promises temporary freedom, spontaneous encounters, reckless decisions, and the outrageous possibility that another person might somehow make existence tolerable. The season eventually ends, of course, leaving everybody to negotiate whatever emotional wreckage remains.

For TWIN ION ENGINE, that dedication provides an appealing premise: romance as an act of cheerful self-destruction, with guitars and synthesizers accompanying every questionable decision. Midsummer Lover invites the romantically afflicted to recognize themselves in its central preoccupation, because whatever else civilization manages to accomplish, people will continue falling hopelessly in love and making spectacular fools of themselves.

items.title: “All the Shadows You Have Inside” — Gothic Rock Veterans The Spiritual Bat Unveil Video for “Theatre of Dust”
items.summary: An old telephone rings in the middle of a forest, resting upon a table draped in red. Nobody seems particularly interested in explaining who placed it there, who might be… The post “All the Shadows You Have Inside” — Gothic Rock Veterans The Spiritual Bat Unve
items.fullText:
An old telephone rings in the middle of a forest, resting upon a table draped in red. Nobody seems particularly interested in explaining who placed it there, who might be calling, or whether answering would be a terrible mistake. Somewhere beyond the trees, a woman searches for an escape from a world that has become intolerably loud, only to discover that silence brings its own troubling questions. After all, how much truth can a person endure before the familiar foundations of reality begin to crumble?

Italian gothic rock veterans The Spiritual Bat explore these uncomfortable territories in their new video for “Theatre of Dust,” the title track of their latest album, released through Swiss Dark Nights. The collaboration between vocalist and lyricist Rosetta Garrì, guitarist Dario Passamonti, and producer and drummer Doc Hammer (Requiem in White, Mors Syphilitica) yields a formidable piece of gothic psychedelia, where personal upheaval and the pursuit of enlightenment collide.

Doc Hammer’s drums establish a steady yet intricate rhythm, providing the foundation for Passamonti’s melodic gothic guitar lines, which seem to draw their power from something elemental. Garrì’s commanding voice rises above the arrangement with an almost incantatory intensity, shifting between vulnerability and theatrical abandon. As the chorus approaches, the music gathers into a baroque surge of  guitars and a bed of icy tones, lending an imposing grandeur to the song’s central struggle.

At its heart, “Theatre of Dust” examines the disorientation of finding everything once considered permanent suddenly rearranged or destroyed. Certainty becomes a casualty of experience, while the search for meaning demands that one confront truths that might be easier to ignore. The song’s concerns feel particularly relevant to an age in which information comes at us relentlessly, yet genuine understanding seems increasingly difficult to obtain.

“‘Theatre of Dust’ explores that precarious threshold where the world shakes around you and forces all hidden monsters and shadows into the open,” says the band. “It is a journey through barren lands and cliff edges, questioning where sanity ends and awakening begins.”

Filmed, edited, and directed by Laura Rossi, who co-wrote the concept with Garrì, the video takes inspiration from the singer’s recurring vision of the Light Seekers, a group of wanderers searching for an elusive Truth. Their journey raises questions about humanity’s tendency to retreat into comforting explanations, even when those explanations bear little resemblance to reality. The desire for enlightenment becomes inseparable from the fear of what enlightenment might reveal.

The film opens with a solitary woman, played by Patrizia Rossi, confined within a dim apartment, surrounded by the relentless intrusion of news from the outside world. Unable to withstand the accumulating pressure, she ventures into the streets before finding herself drawn toward dense forests, ancient stone settlements, and mysterious underground passages. A vintage telephone appears among the trees, a lantern offers guidance, and other seekers gradually join her as the journey progresses.

Rossi’s imagery draws upon the visual language of European folklore and gothic cinema, contrasting the oppressive interiors of modern life with the natural world and the ancient architecture of the Italian countryside. The band appears intermittently, performing within an imposing architectural setting, while a mysterious, witch-like figure seems to preside over the unfolding events. Her increasingly desperate gestures introduce a particularly unsettling possibility: perhaps she wishes to prevent the seekers from reaching the light, or perhaps she knows something terrible about what awaits them.

The pilgrims eventually converge upon a passage illuminated by an overwhelming white radiance, leaving the meaning of their destination tantalizingly uncertain. Throughout the film, the possibility of liberation remains entangled with the danger of discovering something one might wish had remained concealed.

Watch the video for Theatre of Dust below:

The Spiritual Bat’s history stretches back to 1992, when Passamonti co-founded the earlier incarnation Spiritual BatS alongside singer Matteo Bracaglia. Their work developed in close association with the visual arts, particularly the Italian collective I Pittori Alchimisti, whose paintings and alchemical symbolism became integral to the group’s artistic identity. In 1994, Spiritual BatS opened for Rozz Williams and Daucus Karota, an early connection to the international deathrock movement that would become an important part of their history.

With Garrì as vocalist and lyricist, The Spiritual Bat have since established an extensive international following, undertaking multiple American tours and performing at events including Wave-Gotik-Treffen, Whitby Goth Weekend, Return to the Batcave, Castle Party, and New York’s Red Party. Their music draws upon gothic rock, deathrock, post-punk, and psychedelic experimentation, with Passamonti’s distinctive guitar arrangements and Garrì’s expressive vocal performances providing continuity across their recorded catalogue.

Their eight-track album Theatre of Dust, released on August 31, 2026, represents another significant chapter in that evolution. Produced and mixed by Doc Hammer at Goat of Brass Studio in New York, the record also features his drumming throughout. For Garrì and Passamonti, the collaboration carries particular significance, having admired Hammer’s work with Requiem in White since the 1990s.

Across its eight songs, the album considers betrayal, alienation, mortality, human conflict, artistic creation, and the difficult work of finding the strength to carry on. From the personal reckoning of “Hello Heartache” to the societal disillusionment of “Black Fields” and “Babylon Now,” the record approaches these subjects through music that emphasizes emotional contrast and the transformative possibilities of performance.

The video for “Theatre of Dust” offers an absorbing visual counterpart to these ideas, allowing the viewer to follow the seekers toward an uncertain destination and contemplate whether the pursuit of truth ultimately promises salvation, destruction, or some mysterious combination of the two.

Over the course of 15-year career, Toronto-based electronic project Odonis Odonis has worn many hats. True shapeshifters in a diverse scene, the band has always kept their listeners on their toes, whether it be exploring psychedelic dream pop, thrashing through industrial cyberpunk, or exploring those spaces in between, bringing beauty, aggression, and texture to their immense body of work. Now, stripped down to core member Constantin Tzenos, Odonis Odonis has returned with a new barn-burner, titled “No One is Coming to Save You.”

“No One Is Coming To Save You” is the first single from A Fractured Future, the band’s upcoming seventh album. While the band’s 2025 self-titled album was a reflective, moody affair, this track marks a calculated step into acid-house/italo/horror club-centric territory, but with Odonis Odonis’ trademark industrial aggression. As always, the band’s mastery of genres and ability to sidestep through them allows the track to fully succeed in an oversaturated club-centric scene. This move back into caustic, yet danceable territory is by design, as the track’s origins stem from DISORDER, a dark dance night that Tzenos produced with Dwight Hybrid, who also lends production, lyrics, and vocals to the track. “I wanted something that would work at 1am in that room, so I wrote it around the floor first: a hard kick, industrial-darkwave synths and a hook you can shout back,” says Tzenos. “We knew it clicked the first time we dropped it on the dance floor.”

Listen to No One Is Coming To Save You below:

The lyrics for the track are a call to arms against the struggles of modern society. Tzenos adds, “Nobody’s coming to fix this. Not the government, not the algorithm. If you want the world back from the vampires, you have to take it yourself.” Certainly a very prescient theme, especially paired with electronic music’s rich history as a form of resistance.

A Fractured Future has no set release date just yet, but will drop sometime in 2027 on Tzenos’ new After Hours Records imprint.  In the meantime, “No One Is Coming To Save You” can be purchased via Bandcamp and streamed across the internet. Stay tuned for more from Odonis Odonis to come in the new year.
